records.title: PIT derandomization to arithmetic lower bounds
records.statement: Sufficient derandomization of polynomial identity testing implies major arithmetic circuit lower bounds.
hypotheses: The PIT model, field, circuit class and derandomization strength match the theorem.
records.conclusion: An arithmetic circuit lower bound follows.
records.model: arithmetic circuits and polynomial identity testing
residual_hypotheses: Arithmetic lower bounds do not automatically imply classical P!=NP.
The required PIT derandomization is unproved at the needed strength.
records.claim_boundary: Arithmetic-circuit consequences remain a separate model without a proved classical bridge.

records.title: 2026 depth-2 threshold lower-bound frontier
records.statement: A 2026 preprint proves a superquadratic gate lower bound for a function in E^NP against depth-2 linear-threshold circuits.
hypotheses: Circuit model is THR composed with THR.
Quantitative statement and epsilon regime match the preprint.
records.conclusion: The depth-2 threshold lower-bound frontier advances beyond the prior subquadratic barrier.
records.source_locator: ECCC abstract; theorem-level extraction and peer-review status required before composition
residual_hypotheses: Target class E^NP rather than NP.
records.claim_boundary: This is a current restricted frontier result, not a P-versus-NP separation.

records.title: 2026 near-maximum exponential-time circuit lower bound
records.statement: A 2026 preprint proves a near-maximum circuit lower bound for E with promise-MA queries and one bit of advice.
hypotheses: The exact class E^{prMA}/1 and advice/query semantics are retained.
The circuit size measure matches the paper.
records.conclusion: Near-maximum lower bounds are obtained for a strengthened exponential-time class.
records.model: general nonuniform circuits against an exponential-time oracle/advice class
records.source_locator: ECCC abstract; theorem-level extraction and peer-review status required
residual_hypotheses: Target class is far above NP and includes oracle/advice structure.
records.claim_boundary: A strong higher-class lower bound does not settle NP versus P.

records.title: 2026 unconditional AC0-natural barrier frontier
records.statement: A 2026 preprint gives an unconditional quantitative limitation on AC0-computable natural properties for proving certain AC0 circuit lower bounds.
hypotheses: The property is AC0-natural in the paper's sense.
records.conclusion: A localized unconditional barrier applies to that proof-technique class.
records.source_locator: Preprint abstract and headline theorem; exact constants require theorem extraction
residual_hypotheses: Barrier concerns AC0-natural methods and AC0 targets, not all lower-bound proofs.
records.claim_boundary: The result constrains a method class; it is not a general impossibility theorem.

records.title: VP versus VNP algebraic target
records.statement: VP and VNP form an algebraic analogue of P and NP, with the permanent as a VNP-complete polynomial family under algebraic reductions.
hypotheses: Arithmetic circuit model, field, degree and family uniformity are fixed.
records.conclusion: Arithmetic complexity questions and completeness statements are obtained.
records.quantifier_scope: polynomial families over a fixed field
residual_hypotheses: No general theorem equates VP!=VNP with classical P!=NP.
records.claim_boundary: VP versus VNP is a distinct algebraic problem.

records.title: Geometric Complexity Theory programme
records.statement: GCT proposes representation-theoretic and algebraic-geometric obstructions for arithmetic complexity separations.
hypotheses: The selected obstruction is connected to the exact orbit-closure and representation multiplicity statement.
Occurrence or multiplicity obstructions are not assumed to exist.
records.conclusion: A structured route toward algebraic lower bounds is defined.
records.source_locator: Programme formulation; every claimed obstruction requires a separate theorem
records.claim_boundary: A research programme is not a proved separation.

records.title: Circuit-SAT self-improvement frontier
records.statement: Circuit-analysis improvements in one size regime can bootstrap to stronger improvements in another regime under theorem-specific hypotheses.
hypotheses: Circuit size regime, algorithm model and speedup threshold match the theorem.
Randomized or nonuniform variants are not silently changed.
records.conclusion: A circuit-analysis speedup is amplified or transferred within the theorem's regime.
residual_hypotheses: A qualifying initial speedup is needed.
The consequence may be conditional on ETH and does not yield polynomial-time SAT.
records.claim_boundary: Self-improvement amplifies a supplied algorithmic gain; it does not create one.
